entry.title: PICO-8 Beginner Workshop @ A-Lab
entry.content:
Hello everyone,

Our previous Cozy Code session was cozy indeed - thank you all for coming!

Next up, we're back at our usual spot at A-Lab for a beginner workshop on making video games in PICO-8.

You'll need to bring a laptop, but there's nothing to install and no accounts to create. We'll be using the browser-based PICO-8 Education Edition. You'll only need to know the very basics of programming - things like what a function, loop, or if/else condition is.

We'll start with a quick introduction to PICO-8, go through some of the basics of game development and then put it all together by making our own tiny (pico?) game.

There will even be explosions, so we really hope to see you there!

Or if not, catch us on Discord.

entry.title: Introduction to Procedural Music
entry.content:
Hello again creative coders and enthusiasts!

Last time we had a great workshop on image manipulation with p5.js by Adam Driggers (aka @driggs). Thank you to everyone who joined us!

This month we’re happy to welcome Max de Kroon to the stage at A Lab for an introduction to procedural music.

Come join us Sunday, April 26th at 13:00h, at our usual spot at A-Lab .

From Mozart to modular synthesizers, we’ll explore the development of generative music - examining the tools and technologies that allowed this art form to emerge. The goal is to show how seemingly complex compositions are constructed from simple systems of sounds.

Since this is an introductory talk, no prior knowledge of music (or audio) is required. On the contrary, we’ll go over most of the foundational concepts that are true to all genres of music. In the end, we’ll look at one example of a procedural music system made in p5.js

As usual, the second part of the event is dedicated to show & tell. Anyone who wants to show their work on the big screen is more than welcome to do so.

It should be a fun, so we hope to see you there (or online on our Discord).

entry.title: Image Manipulation Workshop with Adam Driggers @A Lab
entry.content:
Hello again creative coders and enthusiasts!

Last time we had a great session reverse-engineering a procedural art piece. Thank you to everyone who joined us!

This month we're very happy to welcome Adam Driggers (aka @driggs) to the stage at A Lab for a beginner-friendly hands-on workshop on image manipulation with p5.js!

Come join us on Sunday, March 22nd at 13:00h at our usual spot at A Lab.

🖼️ Workshop: Image Manipulation with p5.js

Adam will guide you through the surprisingly fun world of working with images in code. Starting from the basics of loading and displaying images, you'll work your way up to pixel-level manipulation and cutting images apart in unexpected ways. Expect to walk away with new tricks up your sleeve and a fresh perspective on what you can do with a photo and a few lines of p5.

Bring your laptop — this is a hands-on session! No deep experience required, just curiosity and willingness to experiment.

After the workshop, there's time and space for some co-working. A great moment to keep hacking on what you've just learned, continue an existing project, or simply hang out with fellow creative coders.

entry.title: Reverse Engineering a Procedural Art Piece
entry.content:
Hello again creatives, coders and enthusiasts!

Last time we had a blast, thanks to Piter Pasma and everyone else who shared their Genuary experiments!

This month we're following up on the beginner workshop from November. Together with Stanko, we'll try to reverse-engineer and rebuild a procedural art piece.

Come join us on Sunday, February 22th at 13:00h, at our usual spot at A-Lab.

Instead of diving into code, we'll explore the ideas behind it - slowly unpacking the patterns, structures and algorithms that make the visuals work. The goal is to show how complex generative art can emerge out of surprisingly simple concepts.

Expect a tour through all kinds of nerdy goodness: Voronoi diagrams, Perlin noise, vector fields, randomness, Chaikin curves, Poisson disk sampling, easings... with interactive examples! No deep math or heavy coding required, just curiosity and a love for creative coding and art!

As usual, the second part of the event is dedicated to show & tell. Anyone who wants to show their work on the big screen is more than welcome to do so.

It should be a fun, so we hope to see you there (or online on our Discord).

entry.title: Genuary Special @A-Lab with Piter Pasma
entry.content:
Hello again curious coders and creatives!

We hope you were able to wrap up last year beautifully and are as excited about the fresh start of the year as we are!

One of the things that gets us excited around this time of year is that fact that the year starts with our favorite month: GENUARY🎉

We're very honored and excited to announce that for our the occasion we'll be joined by none other than the Godfather of Genuary himself: Piter Pasma!

To celebrate, we are organizing a show and tell meetup!

What is GENUARY? It is a month-long event where people use code to make art. You can think of it as a "sketchbook" challenge for anyone who wants to try making generative art. Each day has a different prompt (like "Order and disorder" or "Bauhaus Poster"). It is all about experimenting, sharing cool visuals, and seeing what happens if you push that one parameter up to eleven. You can choose to do all of the prompts, or just select a few you like.

For 2026, Piter Pasma again collected 31 amazing prompts from his friends over at the #genartclub.

For this joyous occasion, we're organizing a GENUARY Special on Thursday, January 29th and this in our beloved spot at A-Lab.

We're planning a big show & tell evening where everybody is welcomed to showcase their GENUARY (or other) work, talk about their inspiration or share their process. Whether you did all 31 prompts or just a few, we'd love to see it! We'll also have space to pull out your laptop and hack away for a bit if you feel like it. Or just sit back, relax, and enjoy the show.

Either way, we think this is going to be a great one! So we hope to see you there!

Or if not, online on our Discord

entry.title: Cityscape
entry.content:
We're launching Cityscape: a community-built, generative artwork made with p5.js.

Run it in your browser and add your own piece of the city via the GitHub repo. If you want to join the challenge, check out the details in the GitHub README.md.

Rules (quick):

  • Canvas size: 3840 × 2160 (4K).
  • Title of the piece: “Cityscape”.
  • Add code, don't remove others' code unless necessary to keep things working.
  • Project caps out at 10,000 lines.
  • Libraries are allowed (try esm.sh for browser imports).

Licensing:

  • Code: MIT.
  • Visual output: CC BY-SA 4.0, credit authors and share derivatives under the same license.

Want help or feedback? Share sketches, questions, or ideas in the Discord #coding-challenge channel, or on your PR. We'd love to see what you can build 🙂

This coding challenge was initiated by Aidan: aidanwyber.xyz

entry.title: Daily Practice Special @ CONTACT MakerSpace
entry.content:
Hello again fellow tinkerers and ponderers!

We really enjoyed our last event at A-Lab and want to thank them for having us, together with everyone that joined us for a wonderful evening!

We're already looking forward to our next event at A-Lab! That being said, this time around we're going somewhere new yet again...

For our September meetup we've been invited by Adam to join him at his place of choice for creative tinkering: CONTACT MakerSpace. Exciting?

Well, if not, we've got plenty more! Adam will tell us all about his daily coding practice and will be joined by Anya, who's bringing us along on her latest Genuary adventure.

We'll wrap up the evening with an open show and tell. Anyone is invited that took part in Driggs' daily practice challenge, no matter how many days you practiced. Even 0 days. If you want to share something, please do!

This time around, there are no chocolates to be won as the challenge kind of is its own prize.

🗣️ Adam Driggers Adam Driggers ("Driggs") will share this his experience of starting a daily coding practice, which just passed the one year mark! He will share some of his sketches, inspiration, successes and struggles. He also present other artists who have developed daily practices and why you might want to start one too!

🗣️ Anya Prosvetova By day she wrangles data, by night she wrangled all 31 Genuary prompts. Data engineer Anya Prosvetova will share her story of starting with creative coding and p5.js through Genuary, a yearly January challenge that invites artists and coders to create generative art based on daily prompts. She’ll share key learnings, sources of inspiration, and practical tips and resources to help you kickstart your own generative art explorations.

💃 Challenge As part of this month's theme of Daily Practice Driggs is inviting/challenging you to start your own daily practice, a short constraint-based exercise.

Many people have found that a daily practice encourages creativity, learning, and growth.

Driggs' tipps for starting a daily practice:

  • Limit yourself to one tool or program
  • Set a time limit. 30 minutes to 1 hour a day
  • Document your work each day
  • Don't try to make each day perfect
  • Make each day self-contained and not just working on a larger project
  • Have fun!

entry.title: Algorithms & Mistakes by Wimer Hazenberg (aka Monokai) @A-Lab
entry.content:
Hello again creative coders and enthusiasts!

Thank you to everyone that showed up for the social in the park last month. We had a great time! As we were just about lucky enough to stay dry then, this month we're heading back indoors. And not just anywhere!

We're very happy and excited to announce that we're welcomed at A-Lab for our August meetup. A-Lab is situated just across the water from Central Station and with their tagline "Where Curious Works" we just had to get in touch. Turns out they're amazing people doing cool stuff and they're happy to have us. We are very grateful for this budding partnership and look forward to grow and nurture it as we go.

But enough about logistics, as we've got more to be excited about! For August we've got another great speaker lined up for you all!

On August 21st Wimer Hazenberg aka Monokai will be joining us at A-Lab for a talk titled "Algorithms & Mistakes".

If you've been anywhere near a code editor in last 20 years, you most probably saw the arguably coolest color scheme 'Monokai' pass by, which was created by Wimer back in 2006. Since then he's built awwwardwinning sites, created stunning 'fog-photography' and most recently has been focusing on Algorithmic Art. Which is also the focus of his talk.

🗣️ Wimer Hazenberg: Algorithms & Mistakes At the core of algorithmic art lies the randomizer. Over-regulate it, and the results become predictable. Let it run free, and chaos takes over. This talk explores how embracing unexpected outcomes can lead to surprising and inspiring creative discoveries.

After the talk, we'll be opening up the floor to admire the results of our very first Space Invaders themed coding challenge. Make sure to enter your entry before August 18th.

We're looking forward to seeing you there!

Guidelines

  • The goal is to create a program related to Space Invaders.
  • Interpret the theme as loosely as you like! Generate invaders or spaceships, make a game, produce some bleep-bloops... raster, vector, 3D, shader, audio, video... space is the limit!
  • Use any programming language and library.
  • Ideally, if it runs on the web, it would be nice to see it live - on openprocessing, p5live, codepen, github pages, netlify... If you need help with this, we can assist.
  • If it is visual, please submit a screenshot.
  • Collaborations are encouraged!

Note regarding the theme - we know that some people struggle to start if the theme is too loose. So, if you feel stuck, here's something more specific:

  • Space Invader generator, 2D or 3D. Use a rectangular grid and generate a random invader in pixels or voxels. Feel free to play with color, size and shape.

Deadline

Prize

We'll do a vote in Discord and whoever gets the most votes wins a box of chocolates! Chocolate will be handed out in person at the next meetup! If you're unable to attend, we'll gladly share chocolates and think of you! :)

Vote is over and Masa's invaders won him the box of chocolates! Congrats!

Hope you'll have fun!

entry.title: May Madness @Mollie
entry.content:
As usual, we'd like to thank everyone who joined us for the Plotter Special last month! Seeing everybody huddled around the plotters was really something...

This month May, as we're invited back at our friends at Mollie's we tried to make it even Madder.

Which is why, we've got not 1, not 2, but 3 amazing speakers for you this time around!

In alphabetical order, we start off with Giedrius Tamulaitis, who's bringing along a peculiarly doomed rotary phone.

Continuing in alphabetical order, we've got Masa, who will take us on a tour through the interactive pixel-art wonder worlds he creates.

And finally, last but not least, still in alphabetical order, we are welcoming Piter Pasma to the stage. He's going to tell us a bit about his work on his "Rayhatcher" algorithm and the use, beauty and magic of SDFs.

Are you excited? Because we sure are! We hope to see you there! Or if you can't make it, come hang out on our Discord.

⚠️ As we've got a packed and exciting program we kindly ask you to try to be punctual so we can get an early start.

📅 Program Details:

☎️ Doom Phone - Coder and artist Giedrius Tamulaitis will tell us a story about turning an old rotary phone into a wireless controller that can be used to play Doom. For no good reason. And you will be able to try it out!

🐰 Interactive Pixel Art - Creative Coder Masa used to draw things like bunnies pretending to be an ice cream, and these days he codes things like dancing meerkats. He will be telling the story of how he started creative coding and share some of his work and the processes behind them.

☀️ Rayhatcher / SDFs - Piter Pasma is a generative artist from Groningen, the Netherlands, who creates three-dimensional artworks using compact mathematical code. Known for his "Rayhatcher" algorithm—line-art-inspired raymarching optimized for plotters. Pasma also fosters creative coding communities through initiatives like Genuary and the collaborative Universal Rayhatcher project. In his presentation he will talk about his "Rayhatcher" algorithm and the use, beauty and magic of SDFs.

entry.title: Plotter Special @Miro
entry.content:
Check the comment for the instructions how to find us in the Miro office!

Hello again creative coders and enthusiasts!

Thank you to those who joined us for our fun and inspiring poetry themed afternoon at CREA last month. While we were just getting comfortable in our cosy corner there, this time around we're going somewhere else.

For our April edition we are invited back to our friends over at Miro's. Well, same friends but a different location as they moved offices last month. We're excited to see where they landed.

What we're even more excited about though, is this month's topic: Pen Plotters! A topic near and dear to us. For those unfamiliar with the term, a 'pen plotter' is a device that holds a pen and can do X, Y, pen up & pen down movement. They come in different shapes and sizes and can also hold more than just a pen. People get very creative with them and even build their own contraptions...

In our upcoming special we'll give a brief overview of the history of plotters and a selection of artists we love, and share some of our own plotter work. However this is also an invitation to you to share what you've seen or made in the space that got you all excited. Anything goes!

To top it all off, there's even more! David and Stanko will be bringing along their AxiDraw's (A3) and we'll be doing some plotting on the spot! If you've always wanted to try and plot something but never got around to it, this could be your chance!

We've made an upload form where you can drop your SVGs. As plotting takes time and our time is limited, we might have to make a selection of what exactly we can plot, but don't let that stop you! We're happy to provide advice or feedback, just drop a note with the upload and we'll get back to you.

Or come and ask your question on our Discord!

For now we'll end with these few resources, The first is an informative article about pen plotting and its history: How Pen Plotting Evolved into a Form of Art - Jared MapleThorpe The second is for if you want to get started but don't know how, this page has a bunch of SVG generators to jump right in: SVG Tools by DrawingBots (Maks Surguy) Or if you want to dive deeper and generate the SVGs yourself, there's a bunch more resources here: How to Pen Plot - Admin :)

Or you can use one of the tools made by David or Stanko for this very purpose :)

entry.title: Poetry Afternoon @ CREA
entry.content:
This time we planned something a little bit different: a Poetry Afternoon!

It is going to be a working session where we gather to create some digital/machine/robot poetry.

What is this digital poetry? You can create an actual poem, or invent a new language, generate an image that resembles a poem, or even a karaoke machine. Feel free to interpret it as you like! It doesn't have to be done by code at all. If you know any poetry nerds, please bring them along!

One little thing, we would prefer if you avoid using LLMs. It is not about asking AI for an amazing poem, but rather about having fun creating and exploring. However, feel free to use AI if you need help with coding.

Some text sources you can use:

  • Project Gutenberg
  • Standard EBooks
  • The CMU Pronouncing Dictionary - A dictionary of English words and their pronunciations, which can be used to generate rhymes.

For inspiration, you can check out the following videos:

  • Making machine poetry with train wagons and OC
  • Comedy Writing With Small Generative Models

We're looking forward to seeing you there, or if you can't make it, come say hi on our Discord

entry.title: Sunday Session @ CREA Café
entry.content:
Hello again creative coders and enthusiasts!

Last month we had an epic event in collaboration with Dance Hack over at Splendor. We want to thank the dance hack crew for co-hosting and especially everyone that showed up and joined us for the workshop. It was a bit chaotic, but fun and engaging for everyone there. Thank you all!

Now for this time around, we're going back to an improved CREA Cafe setting where we've got something planned we've done before, yet a little bit different. We'll be doing a flash-talk on Hydra, the visual live coding environment, followed-up with a themed show and tell.

🕰️ Schedule 13:00 - Start & welcome 13:30 - Hydra Crash Course by David Vandenbogaerde 14:00 - Themed show & tell, theme: Synthesizers

🗣️ Crash Course Hydra by David Vandenbogaerde

Hydra is a browser-based platform for live coding visuals developed by Olivia Jack. The API is inspired by analog modular synthesis, in which multiple visual sources (oscillators, cameras, application windows, other connected windows) can be transformed, modulated, and composited via combining sequences of functions.

David has been developing software for about twenty years now and as the co-organizer of the CCA meetups, it should come to no surprise to you that he likes his coding creative. So when he finally sat down to play around with Hydra in a workshop at C3 earlier this year, it really got under his skin. In this flash talk he'll take you through all the things Hydra he's learned in the mean time, and who knows, maybe pass on the Hydra bug.

🙉 Themed Show & Tell

The theme for this meetup is: Synthesizers. As Hydra was inspired by analog synthesizers, we thought that was the perfect opportunity to have that as the theme. And please interpret as broadly as you like!

Anyone can share a project or thoughts on the topic. This can either be something you did, or something you found interesting. Whatever the topic brings up in you, we'd love to hear and see it!

As for the location, we're heading back to our corner spot at CREA Cafe, only this time we'll be bringing an actual screen on top of the projector. And some curtains probably to make the 'living room' a bit cosier.

Hope to see you there!

Or online, on our Discord
